rows.defeater: Wrong if the write actually reached storage and only the toast was false, or if the stamp call could not realistically fail -- then this is a misleading-message defect rather than a lost save.
Wrong if that tripwire was the only control standing between a shipping money path and a regression -- a control that silently stops testing is high when nothing else covers what it covered.
Wrong if some caller already verified the write independently, or if no provisioned tenant uses course points -- then the false success announcement has no live victim.
Wrong if tools/sairn_sql_preflight.py cannot be absent in any real clone, which would make the fail-open branch unreachable and this a latent rather than a live gap.
Wrong if any independent signal would have shown a zero-app sweep -- a run time, a count, a log line -- because then the clean report was not actually indistinguishable from a real one.

Wrong if the inflated 19 had already been quoted into a plan and diverted real work, or if the same bug also UNDER-counted somewhere, since over-counting is the safe direction and under-counting is not.

Wrong if some other channel independently surfaced the same failures -- a dashboard somebody actually reads, or GitHub mailing the owner -- because then the inert email channel is redundancy lost rather than detection lost.

Wrong toward CRITICAL if a hung fetch is common rather than pathological on the networks these apps run on: 12 apps and ~260 call sites is the widest blast radius in the register, and only trigger-rarity keeps it off critical. Wrong toward moderate if every affected write also persisted locally, so the user loses a message rather than the record.

Wrong if rf_claim_photos was never reachable by a real licensed tenant, or if a downstream human review independently re-verified evidence before any claim was acted on -- then this is a broken control rather than a claim that could be paid on evidence that does not exist.

Wrong toward HIGH if MAX_TOOL_USES_CEILING is large, or if the endpoint can be reached without a licence -- the shape is a spend guardrail failing OPEN on garbage input, and only the small bounded ceiling keeps the consequence modest.

Wrong if a sub_ id is in practice as hard to obtain as a secret, or if Stripe itself re-authenticates the holder before showing billing -- but the record says Stripe puts it in dashboards, webhooks, emails and CSV exports and never treated it as a secret, and the only thing stopping exploitation today is an expired key nobody chose.

Wrong toward CRITICAL if any deployment already runs REPEATABLE READ, because then an overdrawn IOLTA client trust ledger is live rather than one ALTER ROLE away -- and an overdraft on attorney trust money is a reportable event, not an accounting error.

Wrong toward HIGH if the two callers with no handler sit on a write a clinic depends on rather than a vendor convenience -- a dropped socket with no toast is the platform's worst class, and only the narrow scope holds this down.

Wrong toward LOW if a user could work around the refusal, and toward HIGH if anybody responded to the unactionable message by disabling the three-way match itself -- the failure is in the safe direction but the message showed two identical figures and refused, which is how a control gets switched off.
